original_value: One of the most effective methods of limiting air pollution emissions by ships at a berth in a port is the power connection of ships to the on-shore system. “Shore to Ship” (STS)—A universal system for the connection of the ship’s electrical power network with the on-shore network—ensures the adoption of the voltage and frequency of the on-shore network for the exploitation of various types of ships in the port. The realization of such a system is possible due to the use of semiconductor technologies during the construction of mechatronic systems (i.e., systems that ensure the maintenance of electricity parameters). The STS system ensures energy efficiency for high-power ship systems through the use of an active semiconductor converter. This article presents an analysis of steady state electromagnetic and energy processes, allowing the determination of the active and reactive power and losses in the STS system. The presented analytical research enables the development of a control algorithm that optimizes the system energy efficiency. In the article, the control methods allowing the optimization of the energy characteristics of the system are considered and investigated. On the basis of theoretical studies, a model was developed in the Matlab-Simulink environment, which allowed us to study steady and transient processes in the STS system in order to reduce losses in power lines and semiconductor converters.

result.paraphrase: One of the most effective ways to reduce ship emissions while berthed in port is to connect ships to the shore power system. Shore to Ship (STS) is a universal interface linking the ship’s electrical network with the onshore grid, enabling adaptation to the shore supply voltage and frequency for operating different ship types in port. This is made possible by semiconductor technologies used in constructing mechatronic systems that maintain electrical parameters. By using an active semiconductor converter, the STS system improves energy efficiency for high-power ship systems. The article analyzes steady-state electromagnetic and energy processes to determine active and reactive power as well as losses in the STS system. The analytical study supports the development of a control algorithm that optimizes energy efficiency. Control methods for improving the system’s energy characteristics are examined and investigated, and a Matlab-Simulink model was developed from the theoretical studies to analyze steady-state and transient processes in the STS system with the aim of reducing losses in power lines and semiconductor converters.
